subject: Computer Networking
title: What Is Software-Defined Networking?
description: A fast breakdown of What Is Software-Defined Networking? for builders.

hook.text: Traditional networks are configured box by box. SDN controls them all from one brain. A paradigm shift.

buildup.text: SDN separates the control plane from the data plane. Switches forward; a central controller decides.

discovery.text: The controller sees the whole network. It optimizes routing, enforces policies, and reacts in real time.

twist.text: OpenFlow let controllers program switch tables directly. Networking became programmable for the first time.

climax.text: Google's B4 uses SDN to hit 95% link utilization. Traditional networks average 30-40%. Massive gains.

punchline.text: SDN turns networking into software. Program it, don't configure it.

quiz.question: What does SDN separate?
options: The control plane from the data plane

details.summary: Software-defined networking separates the network's control plane from the data plane, centralizing routing decisions in software controllers while switches simply forward packets as instructed.
details.whyItMatters: SDN transforms networks from rigid, manually configured infrastructure into programmable platforms. It enables the automation and agility that modern cloud and data center operations require.
takeaways: SDN separates the control plane from the data plane
A centralized controller programs forwarding rules on switches
OpenFlow was the first major SDN protocol standard

faq.question: How does SDN differ from traditional networking?
faq.answer: Traditional networks embed control logic in each device, configured individually via CLI. SDN centralizes control in a software controller that programs all switches simultaneously.

faq.question: Is SDN widely deployed in production?
faq.answer: SDN principles are widespread in cloud data centers. Google's B4 WAN and major cloud providers use SDN internally. Enterprise adoption uses SDN concepts through SD-WAN and network automation tools.
